task.title: StudyHub 1: fictional message decisions
task.source: Simulation only. You have an existing study-service account and expected a study reminder. You already use the official StudyHub 1 app. Its Help → Report suspicious message route is known. The sensitive request is unexpected. Neither message is conclusively authenticated. All destinations are inert fictional text.
task.brief: Choose actions for both messages and explain each decision. Identify what the evidence supports, what remains unknown, an independent verification route and when/where you would report. Explain what familiar branding establishes. Do not enter real credentials or personal data. A fictional .example suffix is not a scored phishing cue.

messages.text: Your account will close in 30 minutes. Sign in immediately using this message's link.
Your planned study session is today. No sign-in or sensitive information is requested.
messages.destination: No destination or sensitive action requested

criteria.title: Evidence
criteria.standard: Identify the unexpected sensitive request and urgency, threat or scenario mismatch. Suspicion is not conclusive proof.

criteria.title: Safe action
criteria.standard: Avoid the message link and sending sensitive information for both messages.

criteria.title: Verification
criteria.standard: Verify the unexpected request through a pre-established independent trusted route.

criteria.title: Reporting
criteria.standard: Name the known in-app reporting route when suspicion persists.

criteria.title: Reasoning
criteria.standard: Explain why branding does not authenticate a sender and why suspicion is not proof.

criteria.title: Generalisation
criteria.standard: Treat the routine message according to its lower-risk context without claiming certainty.

draft.checklist: The sign-in demand is unexpected and threatens immediate closure. I open my existing official app independently, not the supplied link. If suspicion persists I use Help then Report suspicious message in that app. A logo does not authenticate the sender. These cues support suspicion, not proof.
draft.explanation: The reminder matches my planned session and asks for no sensitive action. I continue without claiming its sender is proven genuine.

variant.content:
Fictional simulation. Phishing asks you to take an unsafe action while pretending to be trustworthy. Inspect the requested action and whether it matches your situation. Branding, polished wording and a secure connection do not authenticate the sender. Pause and verify unexpected sensitive requests through a route you already trust. Report persistent suspicion through the known service channel. An urgent message is not automatically fraudulent.

Separate suspicious cues from proof. Explain remaining uncertainty and select actions suited to each message's context.
